report.answer_text:
In 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi proposed tax cuts and subsidies to ease the cost of living, alongside public investment to spur long-term growth. She outlined the agenda in her October 24 address to parliament, and her cabinet approved a ¥21.3 trillion economic package on November 21. The total rose to ¥25.5 trillion when government investment and loan programs were included. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
Lower household bills. She proposed scrapping the temporary gasoline and diesel tax surcharges, subsidizing winter electricity and gas bills, giving local governments grants for cost-of-living relief, and providing a one-time ¥20,000 payment per eligible child. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
Raise take-home pay. She pledged to raise the income-tax threshold associated with the old ¥1.03 million “income wall.” The tax plan approved by the cabinet on December 26 proposed a ¥1.78 million threshold and a mechanism to adjust key deductions for inflation. Her government also began designing a refundable tax credit for low- and middle-income earners. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
Invest in strategic industries and support wage growth. She proposed using public funding to attract private investment across 17 priority fields, including AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, quantum technology, biotechnology, and aerospace. The plan also called for strengthening critical supply chains and helping smaller businesses invest in productivity so they could raise wages. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
The November package also included a defense and diplomacy pillar, with plans to bring forward defense-related spending to 2% of GDP in fiscal 2025. On monetary policy, Takaichi called for close coordination with the Bank of Japan to achieve its 2% inflation target alongside wage growth, while leaving interest-rate decisions to the central bank. (kantei.go.jp)
